_template_only_note: This file is schema guidance only and must not be copied as an artifact in production. Use scripts/pipeline.py research-prepare, then edit the executable query batch/state as needed.

industry_scope_pack.purpose: Use the scope pack as a boundary card: working/parent/broader market, category classification, reconciliation rules, boundary checks, and research handoff. It is not evidence and must not be converted into findings.

builder_instruction: Do not copy this template as a final plan. First run scripts/pipeline.py research-prepare to generate formal_search_plan.json, coverage_map.json, executable_search_batch.json, and research_graph_state.json together. formal_search_plan is the coverage/evidence-need plan; executable queries are authored only in executable_search_batch.json. Python seeds only starter rows; the configured taxonomy is an LLM expansion menu, and industry_specific_research_threads capture material custom evidence needs.

suggested_issue_menu.instruction: Use these issue_area/subissue pairs as a banker coverage menu, not as a closed ontology. Add material industry-specific rows when the scope requires them; set plan_layer to industry_specific_research_thread and write a clear research_question/evidence_need/source_hint.

planning_instruction: Start from the starter issue rows after reading industry_scope_pack.json. The LLM Query Author may add, drop, rewrite, or reprioritize rows when the industry scope makes them material. Use suggested_issue_menu for banker coverage ideas and industry_specific_research_threads for custom evidence needs; do not force every industry into the menu. For each material entry, write the research question, evidence need, purpose, execution expectation, and source hint. Do not put query/query_variants in this artifact; edit concrete Chinese/English/source-specific query strings only in executable_search_batch.json. Cover must_reconcile items and any boundary_validation_needed questions. Do not write investment hypotheses, validated findings, slide conclusions, target positioning, or page plans. Mark low-relevance rows as accounting/not material during execution rather than forcing equal-depth searches.

issue_search_plan.research_question: What is the current relevant market size for the working market definition, and what is each source's geography/scope?

search_instructions.purpose: Find current market-size datapoints and source scope.
search_instructions.source_hint: official statistics, industry association, company filing, broker or consulting report

issue_search_plan.research_question: Who are the relevant peers and adjacent players that best define this industry footprint?

search_instructions.purpose: Identify peer universe, share indicators, and inclusion rationale.
search_instructions.source_hint: company disclosure, public filing, industry report, analyst coverage

issue_search_plan.research_question: Why does this sector matter for a pre-mandate pitch without turning the industry section into target promotion?

search_instructions.purpose: Collect sector context needed for transaction framing.
search_instructions.source_hint: industry report, strategist notes, transaction precedent context

industry_specific_research_threads.research_need: Find authoritative source-scope evidence before comparing market-size datapoints.
industry_specific_research_threads.why_it_matters: Different category inclusions can make market size and share metrics non-comparable.

research_discipline.execution_report_inherits_plan_taxonomy: In formal_research_execution_report.json, copy issue_area, subissue, and research_question from the issue_search_plan item associated with each executed FS-xxx. Do not reclassify taxonomy in the execution report.
research_discipline.fs_vs_s_id_discipline: FS-xxx IDs are planned search instructions only. After writing this plan, run actual searches and log them as S-xxx entries in artifacts/search_log.md. In the execution report, search_instruction_ids uses FS-xxx and search_attempt_ids uses S-xxx.
research_discipline.if_evidence_is_insufficient: Record the issue/subissue as thin, insufficient, or unavailable_after_research in the formal execution report and research pack; do not invent a page claim.
